title: Add comprehensive logging to plugin audio processor
description: Implement structured logging throughout the audio processing pipeline to aid in debugging and performance monitoring. Logs should include parameter changes, buffer processing metrics, and error conditions without impacting real-time performance.
acceptanceCriteria: Logger implementation uses lock-free queue for real-time thread safety
Log levels (DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR) are configurable at runtime
Performance overhead is < 0.1% in release builds
Logs include timestamps, thread IDs, and parameter states
Log output can be directed to file or console via configuration
Unit tests verify logging doesn't cause audio dropouts
technicalNotes: Use JUCE's Logger class as the foundation. Implement a circular buffer for log messages from the audio thread. Flush logs on the message thread. Consider using std::atomic for configuration flags. Reference: JUCE best practices for real-time logging.

relatedDocuments.reason: Contains JUCE framework patterns and best practices
